newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Firm dollar would boost Dutch exports, inflation.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar would boost Dutch exports, inflation.

text.p: Sustained dollar strength would boost Dutch exports and employment in the short term and reduce the budget deficit, but it would also lead to higher inflation, a spokesman at the government's Central Planning Bureau said.
"A stronger dollar would improve Dutch competitiveness and that would translate into higher exports and increased job growth," the CPB spokesman said.
It would also lead to a lower budget deficit, due in part to higher revenues from gas sales, and to higher inflation as a result of higher prices for imported goods, he said.
The CPB based its most recent public forecasts for the Dutch economy on an exchange rate of 1.70 guilders to the dollar, but the U.S. currency is currently trading at around 1.90 guilders.
For 1997 the CPB forecast Dutch GDP growth of 2.75 percent and consumer price inflation of 2.5 percent.
The spokesman said the CPB would soon begin preparing a new set of forecasts to be published in April, but he declined to say which dollar rate would be used in its calculations.
